description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

PERL: an INVALID sprintf conversion is not a conversion at all -- perl copies
the whole directive to the output LITERALLY (and warns
"Invalid conversion in sprintf" under `use warnings`).  That is how
t/op/sprintf.t asserts rejection: the expected output IS the format text.

PCL: several invalid combinations are formatted anyway.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, probes/p3.pl H3) -- `%v` with a flag between
the `v` and the conversion:

    printf "[%s]\n", sprintf("%v d", "1.2.3");

    perl: [%v d]                      (invalid: left literal)
    PCL:  [ 49. 46. 50. 46. 51]       (formatted as if `%vd` with a space flag)

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/sprintf.t
  227 `>%.3hf INVALID< 'h' should be rejected`
  482 `>%v%,2 INVALID INVALID<`
  494 `>%v#x INVALID<`
and the neighbouring `>%v d<`-shaped rows.  The file drives its cases from a
DATA table whose expected column is literally the word INVALID, so each row is
"does PCL leave this alone".

SHAPE: one place -- the format scanner in `p-sprintf`.  It needs perl's own
rule for what a valid directive is (flags, vector flag, width, precision,
size, conversion, in that order and nothing else between them) and to emit the
matched text verbatim when the scan does not reach a conversion letter.  This
is a NARROWING, so the case it would break is the one to probe: every
currently-working format must still format (the round did not attempt it, so
no A/B exists yet).

Related but SEPARATE: the `use warnings` diagnostic that accompanies it is
`NS:Warnings-gated diagnostics are absent` (#221) and will not close with
this.
subject: an INVALID sprintf conversion must be copied to the output LITERALLY (perl's own way of rejecting it); PCL formats several anyway -- `sprintf("%v d","1.2.3")` is the probe (rows in op/sprintf.t whose expected column IS the word INVALID)
